subsystems.name: Seed code
subsystems.role: the programme that says what to build and in what order.
parts: address tags that mark each piece

subsystems.name: Building blocks
subsystems.role: the molecular units that assemble into the lattice.
parts: monomer units carrying carbon or silicon

subsystems.name: Assembly mechanism
subsystems.role: makes each block find and bind only its intended neighbours.
parts: environmental triggers such as pH, temperature or light

subsystems.name: Energy and feedstock supply
subsystems.role: provides the energy and raw material for growth.
parts: transport of blocks to the growth front

subsystems.name: Error correction
subsystems.role: detects and removes mistakes before they spread.

subsystems.name: Scale-up and integration
subsystems.role: joins molecular lattices into load-bearing structure.
parts: interfaces to conventional foundations and services

buildSteps.title: Design the seed code
buildSteps.detail: Software defines the final form and the binding rules, much as a DNA sequence is designed today for nanostructures.

buildSteps.title: Synthesise the building blocks
buildSteps.detail: Strands or monomers are made in bulk with specific recognition sites, using methods like solid-phase DNA synthesis or protein engineering.

buildSteps.title: Place seed and blocks in the environment
buildSteps.detail: A small seed is positioned where the structure should grow, and blocks are delivered in a fluid or gel medium.

buildSteps.title: Nucleate and grow
buildSteps.detail: The seed triggers ordered attachment; blocks diffuse to the growth front and lock into place.

buildSteps.title: Proofread and repair
buildSteps.detail: Mismatched blocks are selectively released and replaced before growth continues.

buildSteps.title: Terminate
buildSteps.detail: A chemical or physical signal stops assembly once the intended shape is complete.

buildSteps.title: Assemble hierarchically
buildSteps.detail: Many molecular lattices self-organise into larger panels, beams or shells.

buildSteps.title: Integrate with conventional build
buildSteps.detail: The grown structure is connected to foundations, services and conventional materials to form a usable building.

prerequisites.why: DNA origami and self-assembling peptides show the principle, but only at tiny scales.
DNA and protein synthesis provide the building blocks, though cost and purity limit scale.
molecular dynamics can model small systems but cannot yet reliably design a whole growing structure.
a macroscopic material cannot tolerate the error rates of current molecular assembly.
growth in the field would need a local energy source and raw materials without human tending.

pathway.milestone: laboratory self-assembled nanostructures and patterned monolayers
pathway.unlocks: proof that molecules can be programmed to form designed shapes.

pathway.milestone: self-assembling materials that form ordered macroscopic patterns under controlled conditions
pathway.unlocks: first structural materials made by self-assembly rather than machining.

pathway.milestone: seed-triggered growth of simple load-bearing elements in a laboratory
pathway.unlocks: a test of whether assembly can scale beyond microscopic objects.
the speculative vision of structures that grow from a seed — highly uncertain and unproven.
